headline: Airlie holds ALS Limited as a second-order play on rising gold and copper prices via its Commodities testing business, with high incremental margins and no direct cost-base inflation exposure
reasoning: ALS's Commodities segment, roughly half of group earnings, operates a market-leading Geochemistry business with ~30% through-the-cycle returns on capital. Around 75% of Commodities revenue comes from testing services directly linked to exploration spend, which is dominated by gold and copper miners (70% of global exploration spend). Rising gold and copper prices are driving an acceleration in junior miner capital raisings, which Airlie expects to trigger a material earnings upcycle for ALS. During exploration upcycles, ALS requires minimal incremental capital investment to handle higher volumes and gains pricing power, driving incremental margins with returns on capital approaching 40%. Critically, this structure provides gold price exposure without the accompanying cost-base inflation faced by gold miners themselves.
quote: To date, the portfolio has had second-order exposure to a rising gold price via our investment this year in ALS Limited, a global lab-testing company. ALS's Commodities business, which comprises roughly half its earnings, has a market leading Geochemistry business with strong market share and excellent returns on capital (c30% through the cycle). 75% of ALS' Commodities revenue comes from testing services directly linked to exploration spend. Global exploration spend is dominated by gold and copper miners, who account for 70% of total spend. We believe the recent strength in gold and copper prices puts the Commodities business on the cusp of a material earnings upcycle, driven by an acceleration in capital raised by junior miners. During exploration upcycles, there is very little capital investment required for ALS to handle additional volume. These periods are also accompanied by pricing power, all of which can lead to significant incremental margin on sales, and returns on capital that approach 40%. In our view, this business provides exposure to higher gold (and copper) prices without the accompanied cost base inflation that gold miners experience during such periods.

headline: Greencape increased its ALQ position at ~$12/share, seeing the stock as attractively valued with cyclical recovery potential in commodities and underappreciated Life Sciences optionality
reasoning: ALQ's share price has been rangebound for three years despite delivering ~10% EPS growth p.a., driven by declining junior miner sample volumes and the weak performance of the Nuvisan acquisition. During this period, the 1-year forward P/E has derated from 25x to 19x. Greencape views this as attractive for a global leader generating ROE in excess of 20% with a large portion of earnings at what it believes are cyclical lows. The fund increased its position at ~$12/share based on management's track record of outperforming the commodities cycle and the potential for a cyclical recovery as gold and copper prices rise. The market's focus on Nuvisan's weak performance was seen as obscuring the value of the call and put options on the remaining 51% of the business not yet owned, as well as the strong performance of Life Sciences outside of Nuvisan.
quote: During the quarter we increased our position in the company at an average price of ~$12 per share. Our decision was premised on management's continued demonstration of their ability to outperform the commodities cycle, combined with the potential for a cyclical recovery on the back of rising Gold and Copper prices. In the Life Sciences division we felt the market's focus on Nuvisan's weak performance was obscuring the value of both the call and put options management had for the remaining 51% of the business that they did not own (more detail below), as well as the strong performance of the Life Sciences division outside of Nuvisan. In short, the market was looking backwards and putting the group on a low P/E at cyclically depressed earnings.
episode_title: GHCF FR FullReport 202403 1

headline: Views as a high-quality company purchased opportunistically, with temporary headwinds expected to reverse

Greencape expects Nuvisan to no longer be a source of earnings or sentiment drag.
